# Build, Run and Deployment

**Audited commit:** `dbe6d45e7297c5d889be9e69c3e2e190a578e6b1` (branch `main`)
**Package manager:** npm (`package-lock.json`, lockfileVersion 3)
**Workflow:** Expo SDK 57 managed — **no `android/` or `ios/` directories exist**; native projects are generated by prebuild/EAS.

---

## 1. Prerequisites

| Requirement | Detail |
|---|---|
| Node.js | **≥ 22 required.** Not declared in `package.json`, but scripts use `--experimental-strip-types` and `--env-file-if-exists`, which need it. Audited on Node 24.18.1 |
| npm | Ships with Node |
| Expo tooling | Invoked via `npx expo` — no global install needed |
| Android Studio / Xcode | Only for device/simulator builds, not for web or Expo Go |
| `.env.local` | Copy from [.env.example](../../.env.example). App runs without it, but Supabase features are disabled |

---

## 2. Verified commands

These were **actually executed during this audit** on Windows 11 / PowerShell, at this commit.

| Command | Result | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| `npm install` | ✅ **Passes** | 934 packages. `postinstall` ran `patch-package`, applied `onnxruntime-react-native@1.24.3` patch. Reports 22 vulnerabilities (13 moderate, 9 high) |
| `npm test` | ✅ **Passes — 126/126** | 18 test files under `core/`, 0 failures, ~435ms |
| `npm run typecheck` | ✅ **Passes clean** | `tsc --noEmit`, no output |
| `npm run validate` | ✅ **Passes with 5 warnings** | Seed totals: 12 sites, 6 vantages, 10 quests, 3 needs, 5 timeline, 10 plates. Warnings: 5 sites have `coords still 'doc'` (see below) |
| `npm run vocab` | ✅ **Passes clean** | "content and app sweeps pass, and no em dash reaches a reader" |
| `npm run eval:dhamma` | ✅ **Passes 50/50** | answerable 18/18, adjacent 10/10, out_of_scope 12/12, adversarial 6/6, nepali 4/4. **Citations naming an unretrieved passage: 0** |
| `npm run lint` | ❌ **FAILS — 16 errors** | All 16 in one file: [components/monk/SpeechCloud.tsx](../../components/monk/SpeechCloud.tsx). 15 × `react-hooks/refs`, 1 × `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` |
| `npx expo start --web` | ✅ **Serves** | Metro bundles, HTTP 200, ~11 MB JS bundle compiles without error |

> `npm run verify` chains typecheck + test + validate + vocab + eval:dhamma. **It does not include `lint`** — which is why the 16 lint errors can persist while `verify` passes.

### The 5 seed warnings

```
WARN site 'puskarini':      coords still 'doc' — verify against OSM/Wikidata before shipping
WARN site 'marker-stone':   coords still 'doc'
WARN site 'vihara-remains': coords still 'doc'
WARN site 'tilaurakot':     coords still 'doc'
WARN site 'ramagrama':      coords still 'doc'
```

These are **intentional, tracked warnings**, not failures — 5 of 12 sites carry documentation-sourced coordinates not yet verified against OSM/Wikidata.

## 3. npm scripts reference

From [package.json](../../package.json):

| Script | Command | Purpose |
|---|---|---|
| `start` | `expo start` | Dev server, choose platform interactively |
| `android` | `expo start` | *(identical to `start` — does **not** pass `--android`)* |
| `ios` | `expo start` | *(identical to `start` — does **not** pass `--ios`)* |
| `web` | `expo start --web` | Web dev server (port 8081) |
| `dev-client` | `expo start --dev-client --lan` | For a custom dev build, over LAN |
| `api` | `node --env-file-if-exists=.env.local --experimental-strip-types mock-api/server.mjs` | Local mock API |
| `build:development` | `npx eas-cli@latest build --profile development --platform android` | EAS dev build |
| `typecheck` | `tsc --noEmit` | Type check the app |
| `lint` | `expo lint` | ESLint |
| `test` | `node tools/run-tests.mjs` | Core logic tests |
| `validate` | `node tools/validate-seed.mjs` | Seed content integrity |
| `vocab` | `node tools/lint-vocab.mjs` | Project vocabulary/style linter |
| `eval:dhamma` | `node tools/dhamma-eval.mjs` | Dhamma answer-quality eval |
| `gen` | `node tools/gen-data.mjs` | Generate `data/generated/*` from `seed/*` |
| `corpus:fetch` | `node tools/fetch-bilara.mjs` | Fetch the Bilara/SuttaCentral corpus |
| `verify` | `typecheck && test && validate && vocab && eval:dhamma` | The project's health gate |
| `postinstall` | `patch-package` | Applies `patches/*.patch` |

> **`npm run android` and `npm run ios` do not target a platform.** Both run bare `expo start`. To actually launch a platform, use `npx expo start` then press `a`/`i`, or `npx expo run:android`.

## 4. Running the app

### Web (fastest to verify, no device needed) — VERIFIED

```bash
npm install
cp .env.example .env.local     # optional; app runs without it
npx expo start --web
```
Serves on **http://localhost:8081**. Confirmed working at this commit.

> Web is a **partial** experience. Camera, GPS, compass, the MapLibre map, and the on-device damage detector are native-dependent. Platform-split files (`components/map/MapWebView.web.tsx`, `SiteMap3D.web.tsx`) provide web substitutes for the map.

### Expo Go (most features)

```bash
npx expo start
```
Press `a` (Android), `i` (iOS), or scan the QR code.

Per [README.md](../../README.md), most of the app runs in Expo Go, but:
- Camera, GPS and compass need a **real phone**
- The map and the damage detector need a **full build**, not Expo Go

### Development build (all features)

```bash
npm run build:development
# or: npx eas build --profile development --platform android
npx expo start --dev-client --lan
```

### Mock API (optional)

```bash
npm run api          # serves on PORT, default 8000
```
Point `EXPO_PUBLIC_API_URL` at this machine's **LAN IP**, not `localhost` — on a phone, `localhost` means the phone.

| Profile | Distribution | Channel | Android output | Notes |

**Submit config** (`production`, Android): service account key at `./google-play-service-account.json`, track `internal`, `releaseStatus: "draft"`.

> That key file is **not in the repo** and must never be committed. It is excluded via [.easignore](../../.easignore).

```bash
npx eas build --profile development --platform android   # dev client
npx eas build --profile preview --platform android       # installable APK (demo)
npx eas build --profile production --platform android    # AAB for Play
```

## 6. Metro configuration — [metro.config.js](../../metro.config.js)

Two non-default customisations, both load-bearing:

**1. Extra asset extensions**
```js
config.resolver.assetExts.push('wasm', 'opus', 'onnx', 'pte');
```
- `.wasm` — expo-sqlite's web build
- `.opus` — narration audio in [assets/audio/](../../assets/audio/)
- `.onnx` — the damage-detector model ([assets/models/crack-seg.onnx](../../assets/models/crack-seg.onnx))
- `.pte` — reserved for a possible ExecuTorch migration

**If you add a new binary asset type, add its extension here** or Metro will try to parse it as JavaScript.

**2. Cross-origin isolation headers (web only)**
```js
res.setHeader('Cross-Origin-Embedder-Policy', 'credentialless');
res.setHeader('Cross-Origin-Opener-Policy', 'same-origin');
```
Required because wa-sqlite needs `SharedArrayBuffer`. **Removing these breaks SQLite on web.**

## 7. ESLint configuration — [eslint.config.js](../../eslint.config.js)

Flat config extending `eslint-config-expo/flat`, with a substantial hand-written `settings` block restoring React Native platform extensions to the import resolver.

The reason is documented in-source and worth preserving:

> "`eslint-config-expo` carries `import/resolver` in its legacy `default.js` but not in `flat.js`, so under the flat config `import/no-unresolved` falls back to a bare node resolver that does not know React Native's platform extensions. That is why `expo lint` reported expo-audio as unresolvable while `tsc` and a direct `eslint` run both resolved it: same code, two different resolvers."

**Do not delete that settings block** — it makes ESLint resolve modules the way the bundler and compiler actually do. Ignores: `dist/*`.

---

## 8. TypeScript configuration — [tsconfig.json](../../tsconfig.json)

Extends `expo/tsconfig.base`. `strict: true`, `noEmit: true`, `jsx: "react-native"`, path alias `@/*` → `./*`, `allowImportingTsExtensions: true`.

**Excluded:** `node_modules`, `core`, `shared`, `tools`, `mock-api`, `landing`, `scratch`.

The file explains the `core`/`shared` exclusion: they are "device-independent logic with their own typecheck config (`tools/test/tsconfig.json`); they use `.ts`-extension imports and `node:test`, so they are excluded from the app's own include glob. `allowImportingTsExtensions` lets the app's tsc still follow `import ... from '@/core'` when a screen wires the logic in."

> **Consequence:** `npm run typecheck` does **not** type-check `core/` or `shared/`. Those have their own config under [tools/test/](../../tools/test/).

## 9. Deployment

### Mobile app
Via EAS Build → Play Store (`production` profile → AAB → internal track, draft). See §5.

### Mock API
[Procfile](../../Procfile):
```
web: node --experimental-strip-types mock-api/server.mjs
```
Plus [mock-api/railway.json](../../mock-api/railway.json) — deployment target is **Railway**.

### Landing page
[landing/](../../landing/) is a **standalone Next.js app** (its own `package.json` and lockfile) serving the APK download page. It is excluded from EAS builds. It "shares nothing with the Expo project."

Its deployment target is **Needs verification** — it has its own [landing/AGENTS.md](../../landing/AGENTS.md) and [landing/CLAUDE.md](../../landing/CLAUDE.md).

### `.easignore`

Excluded from the build archive: `node_modules/`, `.expo/`, `dist/`, `web-build/`, `landing/`, `docs/`, `google-play-service-account.json`.

> The file notes: "`.easignore` replaces `.gitignore` for the upload, so anything ignored for git that must also stay out of the build has to be repeated here." **If you add a new large or secret directory, add it here too.**

> **`docs/` is excluded** — this knowledge base never reaches a native build, so its size costs nothing at build time.

**No CI/CD configuration found.** No `.github/workflows/`, `.gitlab-ci.yml`, `azure-pipelines.yml`, `Jenkinsfile`, or `circleci` config exists in the repository.

All verification is manual via `npm run verify`.

## 11. Cleaning

```bash
npx expo start -c        # clear Metro cache (also regenerates typed routes)
rm -rf node_modules && npm install
```

> `npx expo start -c` is specifically needed after adding routes — [features/onboarding/steps.ts](../../features/onboarding/steps.ts) notes "Expo regenerates this typed route after `npx expo start -c`."
